Better Tomorrow Ventures
Better Tomorrow Ventures
We invest in exceptional teams we’re excited to work with over decades. Our sweet spot is at the pre-seed/seed when we can lead a round with a $500k - 4M check.
We’ve been founders before and in many ways we’re founders again only instead of writing code, we write checks. This means we’re building BTV on a multi-decade horizon, we work for ourselves and our success is tied directly to the success of the founders we back. We don’t take for granted the opportunity to partner alongside them.
As such, we owe it to tomorrow’s founders to bring the deepest levels of empathy, clarity and rigor to what we hope will be the journey of a lifetime. That means being the first call through the emotionally jagged phases of building and hustling for the things that matter — sparring on product, landing customers, selling talent or just being a consistent sounding board for the things founders cannot share with anyone else. We try to earn our keep on the cap table every day and our founders are usually the best people to ask whether we do.

About Sheel Mohnot
Sheel Mohnot built a distinctive fintech investing profile through two successful exits (FeeFighters to Groupon and Innovative Auctions) plus founding Thistle, giving him unusually deep operating experience that he channels into pre-seed and seed investing at Better Tomorrow Ventures. He's known for his "everything is fintech" thesis, obsession with founder speed and tenacity over specific ideas, and building a large social media following that directly generates deal flow—plus he bootstrapped his first fund by funding early deals from his own bank account before raising institutional capital.
Where they've Worked
This is some text inside of a div block.
Sheel Mohnot's Interests
What they've been talking about across their social media accounts
Tracks late-stage private market valuations and fund performance metrics closely, often analyzing specific returns from firms like Benchmark or comparing cost basis to current trading prices for companies such as Databricks and Ramp.
Focuses heavily on the business mechanics of artificial intelligence rather than just the technology, frequently commenting on revenue growth at major labs like Anthropic or drawing parallels between current skepticism of AI profitability and early doubts about Facebook.
Analyzes fintech mergers and acquisitions with a critical eye for strategic logic, such as questioning the synergy between Southeast Asian superapp Grab and US investing platform Stash, or noting the distribution genius behind Mr Beast acquiring the teen banking app Step.
Shares a strong enthusiasm for food trends and culinary discoveries, ranging from the specific delight of discovering flaky salt on desserts at Square's cafeteria to humorous observations about an Indian restaurant chain named after New York burritos.
Appreciates clever marketing arbitrages and unique business hacks, highlighted by his admiration for an Indian e-commerce giant sponsoring the Namibian cricket team to get cheaper visibility during the World Cup.
Interest in unique real estate and cultural artifacts, evidenced by his personal attempt to bid on the house from the show Breaking Bad and his curiosity regarding how ultra-wealthy families allocate their spending.

Oct 6 •
5 tweets • 2 min read
Bookmark
Save as PDF
My Authors
In Michigan, all public school students take the SAT in 11th grade so you get a full cross-section to look at demographics.
25% of Asians scored above a 1400 (96th percentile) on the SAT; no other demographic comes close
Women scored higher in English (ERW is Evidence-Based Reading and Writing), men scored higher in Math
unsurprisingly parents education levels and median family income are directly correlated with success on the SAT
It is remarkable how much of a bubble we live in. Many working in tech probably don't know many people who scored below a 1400 on the SAT.
The current average SAT at my alma mater (@CarnegieMellon) is 1510.
The whole report is interesting, found here: reports.collegeboard.org/media/pdf/2022…

Walked by this heaping pile of twisted concrete for the 1st time in a while (SF Embarcadero)...
brutalist buildings are bad enough to my eyes but this fountain is the worst example I can think of

Fun fact: U2 performed an impromptu set at the fountain in 1987. They decided to do it with <24 hours notice and ended up being their first cover of "All Along The Watchtower" which they just decided and learned the chords to on the way to the show.

He got fined $500 by the city

456X for seed investors in Figma
They raised $332M in equity and are selling for ~$20B.
Possible they only spent ~$200M of equity capital to get to the $20B outcome.
By contrast Lyft gobbled $7.3B of capital and is worth $5.1B.
Software wins. https://twitter.com/RolfeWinkler/status/1570458596789587968
if this is accurate, OATV sold all of their shares at the series C, meaning they got a 12x return (making some assumptions) instead of the 456x they could have had if they had held on.
